note: Reference example for row filtering — based on the actual bread-demand dataset run where EDA flagged 350 anomalous low-order-count rows as likely non-representative, raised it as a blocking clarification, and the user confirmed they should be excluded. This authorization is what allows Preprocess to filter here — it never infers this from EDA's flags alone.

input.mode_reasoning: first Preprocess call for this dataset — this call handles row filtering and split creation before any feature-level work begins

recommended_strategy.narrative: Exclude the 350 anomalous low-order-count rows (num_orders<10) before training — they are not genuine trading days. Drop num_items_sold, non_bread_quantity, and bread_revenue as features (mechanically tied to the target). day_of_week is a genuine, non-leaky predictor worth engineering directly.

key_findings: 350/3809 rows (9.2%) are anomalous low-order-count records confined entirely to 2015-2023, coinciding exactly with a schema migration — strongly suggesting a system artifact, not real trading behavior

rows_to_filter.reason: confirmed by user clarification (iteration 1, clarification_needed) to be non-representative records (system-migration artifact), not genuine trading days

rows_filtered.reason: confirmed non-representative records (system-migration artifact per user clarification) — removing them before the split so neither train nor validation rows include this anomalous cluster

split_info.note: time-series task (per EDA feasibility) — split is chronological two-way (earliest 80% of remaining rows as train, most recent 20% as validation), not random, so evaluation reflects genuine forecasting rather than interpolation. validation is reused each iteration for Diagnosis's evidence. There is no test partition: the held-out data was removed before this run began and is scored after the pipeline finishes. Created after row filtering, so the anomalous rows never entered either split.

plots.reason: verify the target distribution after removing the anomalous cluster looks like genuine trading-day demand, not a mix of two populations
